claims.text: The superconducting behavior of the as-synthesized Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti alloy is uncharacterized.
At ambient pressure, the alloy exhibits no superconductivity or significantly weaker superconductivity in the accessible low-temperature regime.
Hydrostatic pressure compresses the alloy lattice and reduces interatomic distances.
Pressure-induced lattice compression increases orbital overlap in the alloy.
The increased orbital overlap raises the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Pressure strengthens electron–phonon coupling in the alloy.
Strengthened electron–phonon coupling facilitates Cooper-pair formation.
Pressure-induced electronic and electron–phonon changes cause superconductivity to emerge or become enhanced.
Superconductivity emerges or becomes enhanced after a critical pressure is reached.
Tc increases systematically with pressure up to an optimum.
Above the optimum pressure, Tc saturates or decreases.
Excessive pressure may produce adverse structural changes that reduce or saturate Tc.
The pressure-induced superconducting response is reversible upon pressure release.
Pressures up to approximately 50 GPa can constitute a regime of uniform compression without phase transitions or irreversible structural changes.

contradictions.description: The starting alloy is described as having uncharacterized superconducting behavior, yet the same starting state is said to have baseline measurements showing absent or weakened superconductivity.

Approximately 50 GPa is presented as a safely limited upper pressure intended to avoid phase instability, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that pressure-induced phase transitions may begin below 50 GPa.
